headline: Broadcom in talks for ~$100B AI debt package to fund Anthropic and OpenAI chip capacity
summary: Bloomberg reports Broadcom is negotiating with Apollo and Blackstone on a staged $60B–$70B senior + ~$30B junior debt package (up to ~$100B total) to finance AI compute and datacenter capacity for customers including Anthropic. Broadcom would guarantee part of the senior tranche; debt sits in a separate SPV. CEO Hock Tan has guided AI chip sales above $100B next year. AVGO up ~1% pre-market.

headline: Analog Devices posts record $4.02B Q3 with datacenter revenue +100% YoY; buys Empower Semi for $1.5B
summary: ADI reported fiscal Q3 revenue of $4.02B (+40% YoY, first quarter above $4B), driven by data center and industrial. Data center now ~80% of the communications segment, with optical and power businesses each up more than 100% YoY. Adj gross margin 72.5%, adj op margin 50.0%. ADI also announced a $1.5B cash acquisition of Empower Semiconductor targeting power delivery for AI accelerators. JPMorgan reiterated Overweight, calling the print a signal that AI datacenter growth is outpacing expectations. Positive read-through for VRT, ETN, GEV and optical suppliers (GLW).

headline: Alibaba Q2: revenue +9% but profit -75% as AI capex surges to CNY 67.7B (+75% YoY)
summary: Alibaba reported June-quarter revenue of RMB 269B (+9% YoY) but operating income -57% and net income -75% as the company plowed cash into AI infrastructure. Capex jumped ~75% YoY to CNY 67.7B against its RMB 380B multi-year AI infra plan. AI Cloud & Compute Services grew 45% to RMB 48.4B; AI-related product revenue hit RMB 12.4B. EPS $1.26 vs. $1.85 consensus. ADRs fell ~3%. Reinforces the global read that hyperscaler AI capex is accelerating, not decelerating — bullish demand signal for NVDA/AVGO/AMAT/LRCX/KLAC and HBM (MU, 000660.KS, 005930.KS).

headline: Wolfe Research reiterates bullish AI-semis call, names NVIDIA top pick into Aug 26 print
summary: Wolfe Research told clients it remains broadly bullish on AI semiconductor stocks and picked NVIDIA as top idea heading into next Wednesday's fiscal Q2 report. Street expects $93B–$95B revenue vs company guide of $91B ±2%; Goldman Sachs sits 6% above consensus on FY26 EPS and 19% above on FY27. Blackwell ramp and Vera Rubin partner availability in 2H26 remain the near-term catalysts.

headline: Intel slides third straight session after Socionext picks 18A-P for HPC/datacenter chiplet
summary: Japanese fabless Socionext said it will use Intel's 18A-P process for a new high-performance compute chiplet targeting datacenter, HPC and edge. It's a foundry win for Intel — but not exclusive — and the market read was muted: INTC fell for a third straight session (closed $92.13, -0.7%) and Socionext shares dropped 5.4% in Tokyo. Investors continue to fade Intel Foundry customer announcements without volume disclosure.

headline: US indices closed lower Aug 20 on Treasury yield spike; futures pointing higher into Powell at Jackson Hole
summary: Thursday closed with the Dow -1.32% to 52,759, S&P 500 -0.87% to 7,641 and Nasdaq -1.0% to 26,067 as long-end Treasury yields backed up despite the Treasury's expanded buyback operation. Walmart -9% weighed on the tape after a weak comp and cautious FY guide. S&P futures were +0.3% and Nasdaq futures +0.5% pre-open Friday with focus shifting to Powell's Jackson Hole address for tone on the September FOMC.

headline: Applied Materials Q3 beat but soft Q4 guide keeps semi-equip stocks under pressure
summary: AMAT's Q3 EPS of $3.50 (vs $3.39) missed the elevated expectations bar on light Q4 revenue and margin guidance given last week. The read-across pulled LRCX and KLAC lower. Contra-signal: Lam CEO Tim Archer said 2026 WFE spending is tracking to the low $150B range vs a prior $140B outlook, with upside bias. Chip-equipment complex trades on customer capex, not near-term guides — TSMC $52B–$56B, ASML raised to €43B–€45B, and hyperscaler capex on pace for ~$700B in 2026 remain the trump cards.

headline: CoreWeave 3-session slide continues despite $104B backlog and 1.85 GW YE power target
summary: CRWV is off ~16.5% over the past three sessions even after last week's Q2 print showed record $2.6B revenue (+112% YoY), a $104B revenue backlog, a raised FY26 revenue guide to $12.4B–$13.2B and a lift in year-end active power to more than 1.85 GW. Concerns center on the $35B–$39B FY26 capex, rising leverage, and margin drag from the fastest datacenter buildout in the sector. Watch as a leading indicator on AI infra funding costs.
